posts.cooked:
Ok, silly fanficy idea I came up with after hearing about the Church of the Dawn.

Kathrine was born to 1 of the superpowered church leaders but had no powers, which her parents saw as a divine punishment and mistreat her as a result. Eventually she runs away and becomes a kick-ass laser gun-wielding vigilante named ExcommuniKate.

Nothing like a good excuse for a combined pun and homage.

Hope we get space for more of this universe. There’s as much potential here as the Inversiverese and Xtremeverse; perhaps moreso since you’re not exclusively limited to adapting Universe-1 characters (though all the magic characters being dead probably closes the gap).

Wonderful episode.

I was definitely hoping for “Legacies of Tomorrow” as the title of the comic; it covers multiple Legacies, but also how a bunch of the other characters are also legacies in different ways, and it’s in the future, and it sounds comic book. I would back a Neon Necromancer writer’s room (and an entire addition of a Neon Necromancer limited series.)

I used to say I lamented Sentinels couldn’t really have a “surprise kids from the future” story because of the way time travel works, but this does have some of the same vibes.

I had a good sympathetic chuckle at the bit where Christopher really wanted to engage in some serious alternate history crafting, but Adam had to point out comics don’t do actual proper AH crafting, lol.

I love how in keeping with Argent Adept being something of a butt monkey in a meta-meta sense, that the Neon Necromancer is someone who would drive him up the wall and result in a lot of grumbling.

I totally need all the arts for all the new characters created in this.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Sea-Envy:

when I said 1999 writers, I meant that when this book came out no one knew that La Camadora is the reason Haka is immortal.

That’s a good point. In 1999, they probably would have assumed it was magic of some sort, and by rights he should have been dead. There would be no reason to ascribe it to cosmic shenanigans.

Powerhound_2000:

It’s mentioned one of the powers is “silver form” but it’s never really explained.

I was confused by that, too. They clearly understood it with no explanation, but I don’t see that it’s a standard comic book term. I don’t think it’s like Colossus, or else it would convey toughness like Lantern’s, and she’s less tanky. Silver Surfer’s form is just sort of general cosmic-ness; the silver itself is cosmetic. I thought Silver Samurai had some silver-related power, but no, it’s just his armor (his power is energy focusing through his sword). Beacon is definitely reflective, but that’s all I got out of it. I think I’ll ask when I write my follow-up letter.

TakeWalker:

So we need six Writer’s Rooms for this series, is what I’m hearing.

A least seven, to cover the Disparation re-visit by La Comodora. And it seems there may have been more than one of those.

posts.cooked:
Infinite Legacies

But seriously, they belabored the name for way too long. I’m still impatiently waiting for them to tell a story.

Paahl and Fae’Lisha

I don’t know how they decided on the splitting up the powers, but I’m far more interested in the story of their mother, the most powerful Legacy ever who has 20 different powers, than in the two twins with 10 each and 1 they both have.

Their villain is Barron Morden, and Mordengrad is now the entire moon.

You still have bank robbers, but now they rob the gene bank, which is where there are all the designer genes that give you Cyclops eye beams.
